title: 2024 budget approved; short-term rental review launched
subtitle: Highway 6 planning, Lamond Street heritage designation, Ainley subdivision servicing, Enbridge franchise, Integrity Commissioner report and 820 St. David St. N. rezoning.
overview: At its last meeting of 2023, Council approved the 2024 budget as amended by the Committee of the Whole. Changes included directing the 2024 OLG funds to the termite management program, phasing in the pay increase for Members of Council over 2024 and 2025, adding tennis to the Parks and Recreation Master Plan, and an interest-free loan to the Elora BIA. Council also asked staff to look into the profitability of the Fergus Grand Theatre.

On short-term accommodations, Council chose a two-step approach: public consultation and an inventory of active rentals, then a draft licensing by-law. Staff said parking work comes first, so no new rules will be in place for the coming tourist season. Council also asked the province to work with the Township on the future design of Highway 6 in Fergus, including sidewalks, multi-use paths and roundabouts.

Council designated 255 Lamond Street under the Ontario Heritage Act, approved a rezoning at 820 St. David St. N., and authorized a servicing agreement for the Ainley subdivision. It also approved the Enbridge Gas franchise renewal, and ordered the Integrity Commissioner's report posted online. The closed session was cancelled and its matters deferred to January 2024.

decisions.item: 2024 budget and Committee of the Whole report
decisions.detail: Council approved the 2024 budget as amended, including the 2024 business plan, fees and charges, a phased pay increase for Council and an interest-free loan to the Elora BIA {{vote:m3}}.
Council directed staff to consult the public and inventory active short-term rentals, then draft a licensing by-law and enforcement strategy, with reports back at each stage {{vote:m17}}.
Council directed staff to start talks with the Ministry of Transportation, supported active transportation facilities in Fergus, and encouraged roundabouts at two intersections {{vote:m16}}.
Council confirmed the property's designation as having cultural heritage value under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m6}}.
Council found no further public consultation was needed and approved the amended rezoning application RZ05/18 {{vote:m11}}.
Council authorized a service financing agreement with the developer for required services on Gerrie Road and Colborne Street {{vote:m7}}.
Council approved the draft franchise by-law and agreement for submission to the Ontario Energy Board and asked that elector assent be declared unnecessary {{vote:m14}}.
Council directed that the written reasons in the Integrity Commissioner's November 16, 2023 report be posted on the Township website {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On short-term accommodations, several councillors favoured the licensing option, citing the loss of long-term rental housing, neighbourhood impacts and a possible municipal accommodation tax. Some suggested pairing the work with the 2024 tourism master plan.

Staff said they are mindful of capacity and want to put parking strategy recommendations first. They said consultants with different expertise might be needed for the rental and tourism projects. One councillor asked about interim controls for the coming tourist season, and staff confirmed none would be in place.

On Highway 6, staff said a coordinated plan would be more efficient than reviewing each development application separately. They noted the Ministry's 14-metre setback and noise-mitigation requirements complicate road design. Councillors raised transit, parking and active transportation, and one stressed the safety of the Wellington Road 22 intersection.

On the 820 St. David St. N. rezoning, a councillor supported intensification but worried that housing would sit close to a gas bar and drive-through because a lot line separates them. Staff said the gas bar is on a separate property and that safety regulators identified no separation standard. Councillors asked for tree buffering at site plan and for variety in housing design.

During the Integrity Commissioner's presentation, councillors asked about conflict-of-interest exceptions, whether the whole Council would have to step aside on a widespread issue, and when repeated applications can be treated as frivolous. The Commissioner said each must be reviewed before it can be dismissed.
